claims.feature: Multi-GB streaming (files read from disk in slices)
tests: ui:log-analyzer:2.13: a 60 MB log streams through a Worker; counts and timeline cover it all and grep scans the whole file
unit:stream:lines: time grows linearly with the lines in a chunk (no quadratic queue; the Log Analyzer read 50 MB at 4 MB/s)
ui:log-analyzer:A5: a dropped log file is read (encoding detected) instead of failing
ui:log-analyzer:B7: a stack trace belongs to its log line: counts, filters and export are per event
unit:logs:splitEvents: continuation lines join the event before; counts events, not lines

claims.feature: Parsers: JSON, key=value, Apache/Nginx, syslog, Windows events
tests: ui:log-analyzer:2.13: JSON, logfmt, syslog and Windows logs: level, time and fields are read; a line shows its fields
unit:logs:detectFormat: JSON, logfmt, access, syslog 3164 and 5424, Windows, plain
unit:logs:parseEvent: fields, level and time for each format
unit:logs:parseTime: ISO, Apache, syslog, Windows, epoch seconds and milliseconds
ui:log-analyzer:2.13: timeline histogram; dragging across it zooms the list to that time range
unit:logs:histogram: nice bucket sizes, counts per level, empty span handled
ui:log-analyzer:2.13: several files are merged by time, each line tagged with its file
unit:logs:mergeByTime: k-way merge, ties keep file order, untimed events stay after their predecessor
ui:log-analyzer:2.13: saved searches and highlight rules are kept for next time
